 Fewer Americans Will Host Thanksgiving as Inflation Reshapes Menus and Shrinks Guest Lists
 News provided by
 LendingTree, Inc.
 Nov 16, 2026, 16:01 ET
 Share this article
 Share this article
 LendingTree's 2026 Survey Finds Thanksgiving Hosts Expect to Spend $427 as Nearly Two-Thirds Say They May Need to Borrow 
 CHARLOTTE, N.C. , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fewer Americans say they may host Thanksgiving this year, while those considering hosting expect to spend more, according to LendingTree's 2026 Thanksgiving spending survey. Just over half of Americans (51%) say they might host, down from 59% in 2025. Potential hosts expect to spend an average of $427 on food, drinks and housewares, up 3% from $414 last year.
 The survey of 2,000 U.S. consumers finds that inflation is affecting the Thanksgiving plans or budgets of 53% of those planning to celebrate. A quarter (25%) are changing food choices, 22% are using more coupons and 14% are cutting back on guests. Among potential hosts, 32% say hosting is a financial strain and 78% have a budget.
 Even with budgets in place, 62% of potential hosts say they may need to borrow to cover the festivities. Guests may also be asked to help: 60% of potential hosts expect contributions of money, food or drinks, and 25% would consider leaving a non-contributing guest off next year's invitation list.
 Key Findings 
 Fewer Americans may set the Thanksgiving table.  51% say they might host in 2026, down from 59% in 2025 and 56% in 2024. Potential hosts expect to spend $427 on average, up from $414 last year but slightly below $431 in 2024. Parents of children younger than 18 (67%) and six-figure earners (66%) are among the most likely to consider hosting.
 Inflation is reshaping menus and guest lists.  53% of Thanksgiving celebrators say inflation is affecting their plans or budget, including 25% changing food choices and 14% cutting back on guests. Among potential hosts, 32% say hosting is a financial strain, while 78% have a budget, including 25% who say it's strict.
 Borrowing may be on the Thanksgiving menu.  62% of potential hosts say they may need to borrow, including 38% who plan to use credit cards and 18% who plan to use buy now, pay later loans. Among those planning to charge hosting expenses, 89% expect to pay off their balances within three months, including 56% within a month.
 Come empty-handed and next year's invitation could be off the table. Potential hosts expect to welcome an average of 10 people, and 60% anticipate guests will offer money or bring food or drinks. A quarter (25%) would consider leaving a guest off next year's list for not contributing, rising to 46% among Gen Z potential hosts.
 To view the full report, visit:   https://www.lendingtree.com/credit-cards/study/thanksgiving-cost-report/  
 LendingTree's Chief Consumer Finance Analyst, Matt Schulz, says the cost of hosting is a burden for families:
 "Thanksgiving is supposed to be about coming together, but the cost of doing that is becoming a real concern for many families. People are changing their menus, inviting fewer guests, and looking for ways to stretch their dollars. What's especially troubling is how many hosts may need to borrow money just to cover the celebration. A holiday meal can be expensive enough on its own. When you add credit card interest or other borrowing costs, that one day of celebrating can end up costing you for months afterward."
 Methodology
 LendingTree commissioned QuestionPro to conduct an online survey of 2,000 U.S. consumers from Oct. 2 to 9, 2026. The survey was administered using a nonprobability-based sample, and quotas were used to help ensure the sample reflected the overall population. Researchers reviewed all responses for quality control.
 Generations were defined as follows in 2026: Generation Z, ages 18 to 29; millennials, ages 30 to 45; Generation X, ages 46 to 61; and baby boomers, ages 62 to 80.
